newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Acacia optimistic for stronger profit.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Acacia optimistic for stronger profit.

text.p: Acacia Resources Ltd said on Wednesday it was optimistic of achieving a stronger profit in calendar 1997, although it said the first quarter had been challenging.
Acacia said it expected gold production of over 350,000 ounces in calendar 1997, compared with production of 267,392 ounces in 1996.

"Overall despite difficult conditions (in the first quarter) we are optimistic that a strengthening of our profit result will be achieved in 1997," chairman Peter Wade told shareholders at the annual meeting.
The company, which was spun-off from Shell Australia three years ago, achieved a 1996 net profit of A$14.34 million from A$22.13 million in 1995.

"Production and revenues production in 1997 is expected to exceed 350,000 ounces, in line with previous forecasts, despite the adverse affect of record rainfall on production from Acacia's Northern Territory operations during the quarter," the company said in its accompanying quarterly production statement.

Acacia said its March quarter gold output of 66,408 ounces was 10 percent below the December quarter record of 73,920 ounces due to the adverse wet season. Operations were now back to normal and record quarterly production was expected in the June quarter with the first output from the Sunrise Dam.
